messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — proposing a compact-claims gateway to shrink API key surface and speed auth checks. Thoughts?
ben: Short version: one broker that rewrites wide claims -> compact internal claims, less header bloat.
sasha: Why a gateway vs library? we lose some observability if opaque.
elaine: Gateway gives centralized rotation & caching, and lets downstream services validate a small fixed schema instead of evolving claims.
tom: Concern: single-point-of-failure + HA complexity. are we counting on infra for that?
elaine: yes, it would be behind our load balancer and deployed replicated in every region. fallbacks to legacy validation for outages.
infra-bot: deploy-check: gateway must expose /health, /metrics, and token-cache-miss rate tag.
maria: Also need policy for claim contraction: which fields allowed to be dropped or hashed. sample: `user_id`, `roles[]` -> keep, `org_tree` -> hash.
ken: Can we see a tiny example transformation?
elaine: example input token claims (simplified):
```
{
  "sub": "svc:payments:123",
  "roles": ["pay:write","pay:refund"],
  "org": "org:acme>team:billing",
  "env": "prod",
  "exp": 1713000000
}
```
elaine: output compact claims might be:
```
{ "s":"svc:payments:123","r":"a1","o":"h3","e":1713000000 }
```
elaine: where `r` and `o` are stable small enums / hashes and gateway maintains mapping and TTL.
sasha: mapping table is effectively additional state. how do we handle invalidation when roles change?
elaine: gateway listens to role-service events and invalidates mappings; we can also embed a short `version` field in compact token.
ben: performance numbers? if gateway adds 3-5ms every call it could be bad for hot paths. can we cache on edge?
elaine: plan: LRU local cache in each pod + CDN edge caching for long-lived mappings. cache hit -> <1ms, miss -> 4-8ms depending on mapping.
tom: opt: offer two modes: "inline contraction" library for extremely latency-sensitive services, gateway for everything else.
maria: Security review: contraction must be deterministic and collision-resistant for hashed claims. also consider forward secrecy for mappings.
ken: How does this affect RBAC checks? would policies accept compact values or require gateway to expand on demand?
elaine: idea A: services accept compact claims and RBAC engine understands compact enums/hashes. Idea B: gateway can (optionally) expand into full claims for policy engines that need them.
sasha: Idea A reduces bandwidth and parsing. Idea B easier for incremental migration. Prefer B for rollout.
olivia: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) deploy gateway in read-only mode (observability + no rewrite) 2) opt-in downstream to accept compact tokens 3) provide expansion API for a period 4) flip default.
ben: Ops note: need to rate-limit expansion API to avoid amplification attacks.
ken: Testing: add synthetic perf suites + role-change churn sim to validate invalidation logic.
elaine: Good call. I'll draft a follow-up doc with mapping schema, TTLs, and rollout steps. Anyone want to co-author?
sasha: I can take the mapping/invalidation section.
ben: I'll own perf/latency measurements and tests.
mar ia: (typo) -> maria: I'll run the security checklist and threat model.
elaine: thanks all. if no blockers I'll open the design doc PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
